purpose: Test whether a reader can choose an appropriate tool, reach a first useful result, and interpret it using the visible wiki and its linked instructions.
user_priority: Useful and easy to work with.
method: Three fresh-context subagents independently simulate one reader task each. The coordinator checks actionable findings after their first walkthrough.

scenarios.task: Check a small Python project for coding and type mistakes on Windows.
Find and test a disposable HTTP API, including invalid inputs or server errors.
Investigate a crashing native C/C++ program on Windows with source and rebuild access.

constraints: Start at the home page without prescribed tool choices.
Do not read source, previous audits, or other reports to discover the route.
Use visible wiki text and its explicit links before relying on outside knowledge.
Record exact navigation, commands, output and missing instructions.
Use synthetic inputs and isolated local environments only.
Keep product files and existing audit records unchanged.
success_criteria: Select suitable tools and explain their scope.
Find prerequisites, inputs and a complete procedure.
Obtain a first meaningful result where the environment permits.
Interpret findings, setup failure and clean results separately.
Find a correction or next action and a way to retain/reuse the procedure.
classification: Completed with documented recovery or outside knowledge
Blocked by environment or testing infrastructure
limitations: These are expert-agent walkthroughs, not observations of human readers.
No claims about human completion times, emotions or population-wide usability.
Three scenarios do not cover the whole catalog or accessibility conformance.
initial_harness_issues: Background preview processes ended unexpectedly; the coordinator restored isolated loopback servers serving unchanged dist. Initial connection failures are not product findings. One agent retained its original origin after an automatic navigation approval rejection; no rejection was bypassed.
method_corrections: A pinned-only dependency restriction was removed during the Python walkthrough. Explicitly linked official install commands are allowed in a fresh local environment; actual versions must be recorded. Lack of a version pin alone is not a usability failure.
The initial preview startup failure and one rejected origin change are testing infrastructure events, not product findings.

result_summary.python: Demonstration completed; actual project adaptation not executed.
result_summary.api: Demonstration completed in a labeled Python 3.13 recovery; exact 3.12 setup and own-API adaptation remain untested.
result_summary.memory: Selection and interpretation assessed; no diagnostic run because readiness/compatibility was unresolved and tools were unavailable on PATH.

cleanup.retained_execution_roots: Ignored .preview/reader-usability contains the fresh environments and raw evidence; no global tools were installed.
